chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Ziyād, from Manṣūr ibn Yūnus, from al-ʿAbd al-Ṣāliḥ عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him saying: “When the sun passes the meridian, then the time of the two prayers has entered.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose movement marks the prayer time
key_terms.الصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two prayers, meaning ẓuhr and ʿaṣr in context
key_terms.الْعَبْدِ الصَّالِحِ: a title for the Imam عليه السلام in the chain
key_terms.زَالَتِ: passed the meridian; declined from the zenith
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time for an act of worship

ai.seo_question: When does the time of the two daytime prayers begin in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when the sun declines from its zenith, the time for the two daytime prayers begins. It indicates a legal ruling concerning the beginning of the prayer time for ẓuhr and ʿaṣr.
